name: libxsmm-full512-column-panel-first-traversal
hypothesis: Interchange the full512 traversal: sixteen 32-column panels become the outer loop, with eight 64-row blocks inside each panel. Both 32-row halves stay together. Each row block packs its current A rows before both consumers, then advances A and C by 131072 bytes. After eight blocks, rewind A and C by 1048576 bytes and advance B and C by 128 bytes for the next column panel. B remains at the current panel throughout the row sweep. This tests B-panel reuse while increasing A packing from eight to 128 packs per GEMM; benefit is unverified. This differs from the measured row-half-first traversal and packed-B layout. The 512-step reductions, FP32 order, scratch layout, SME transitions, general-size fallback, n<=0 behavior, unused helper and both complete license notices remain unchanged. No tools or tests were run. Compilation, full-GEMM correctness and fresh repeated paired performance checks remain required under the unchanged gates and initial power settings. No speedup or throughput above 1800 GFLOP/s is established.
